finalMessage:
I moved the password hash in `Login` ahead of the lockout check in `accounts/session.go`, so a locked account now does the same hashing work as a wrong password before it is refused. The change is uncommitted.

**Risk-relevant item touched:** `R-LOGIN-LOCKOUT` (`accounts/session.go#Sessions.Login`). It is still true. A locked account still gets `ErrLocked`, the failure counter is untouched, and a correct password is still refused while locked. Only the timing changed. I did not edit the item text. It controls `RISK-ACCOUNT-TAKEOVER` and refines `N-ACCOUNT-SAFE`. Please have a second reviewer look at this item in the PR.

**Tests:**
- `TestLoginLockout` (verifies `R-LOGIN-LOCKOUT`) passes, as do `TestLogin` and the rest of `./accounts`.
- `ostf check --base main` exits 0. It reports one info line about two unlinked items, `R-ORDER-NOTE` and `R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT`, which this change doesn't touch.
- I did not add a timing test. Timing parity is hard to assert reliably in a unit test, so the change is verified by reading only.

**Not addressed:** An unregistered email still returns `ErrBadCredentials` immediately, without hashing. A registered email with a wrong password takes the full PBKDF2 time, so response timing can still reveal whether an email is registered. Your approval covered only the locked-account case, so I left this alone. Say the word if you want a dummy hash on that path too.
